description: Candidate manifests harvested from Wikidata structured data and Know Your Meme confirmed sitemap. Company and title candidates remain source-backed candidates; per-record scope notes and provenance retained. See checkpoint for tiering limitations.

company_metadata.source: Wikidata Query Service; P452 selected technology sectors + direct company/business class; excluded P452 industry ancestry Q941594 and P31 ancestry Q112042224; English label/description, P856 homepage.
boundary_notes: Explicit game-industry company classifications are filtered out. A company with a separate unmodeled gaming division may slip through; only primary business data plus game-industry flags can be assessed at this scale.

Wikidata item links and P452/P31 statements are item-level provenance; P856 values link to official company pages where recorded. The official page links were not individually opened for all 5k+ records.
This is a structured dataset harvest and should be spot-checked in country/industry batches before any central-bank import.

Additional name/description screen excludes 239 candidates whose English item descriptions identify video game publishing/development, gaming companies, console/Pong-console manufacturers, or iGaming. Ambiguous short labels that collide with major game-company names (for example EA, Supercell) are excluded even when the matched Wikidata item has a different local-company identity.

meme_metadata.method: Stream-downloaded the robots.txt-listed XML sitemap; extracted only URL paths, excluded /sensitive/ entries, derived a readable answer label from the final URL slug, and deduplicated normalized labels against the current full answer set and /tmp/megabytle_large_memes.json. Used each sitemap URL as the source link. No article descriptions, images, or post content copied. Slug-derived titles are candidates; verify human casing where needed.
meme_metadata.notes: Sitemap itself lists 23,632 unique URLs, including 2,298 under /sensitive/; imported candidates are the remaining non-sensitive /memes/ records that were not already in the current bank or candidate manifest.

tech-company-games-company.method: Ranked by Wikidata sitelink count descending; 15% deep-cut allocation among final set; source limitations retained in each answer.

internet-meme.method: Know Your Meme robots-listed confirmed sitemap; labels slug-derived; tier allocation balanced, not popularity-ranked.

additional_candidate_batches.source_rule: Human entities linked as founder (P112) or chief executive (P169) from the tech-company candidate set; role and company QID retained per record.

additional_candidate_batches.method: Started from Wikipedia’s public “List of fictional hackers” and “List of fictional scientists and engineers” lists, then checked candidate-specific Wikidata items for fictional-character identity and relevant occupations/aliases and compared against the app bank. This is broader than direct occupation-only retrieval and admits documented roles from the curated list while holding weak fits as borderline.
limitations: The Wikipedia lists are explicitly dynamic/incomplete and some entries are weakly sourced; inclusion there alone was not treated as sufficient. Each accepted row also has an item page and an explicit role/occupation statement or list-plus-character-page evidence.
Wikidata statements are uneven in sourcing; this candidate harvest is not a popularity ranking and leaves obscure/ambiguous characters out or in borderline.
No central answer-bank files were changed.
